detailed_description:
LOCATION MAP: The crossroads of two muddy roads in open winter pasture. THE TREE, a single ancient leafless oak, stands at the right-hand front corner of the crossroads; its thick LOW LIMB runs almost horizontally out over the verge toward the centre of the crossroads. A rough LADDER leans against the trunk on the road side. The low HITCHING POST stands in the same verge a few paces from the trunk. At the foot of the tree, among the huge knuckled ROOTS, the earth is black, soft and bare. THE BACK ROAD enters at the far left round a BEND hidden by a bare thorn HEDGE; THE ROAD AHEAD leaves to the right, straight, long and open; THE OPPOSITE ROAD comes down toward us from a low bare HILL far behind. Nothing else stands in the open fields. Camera side: the camera stands on the back-road side of the crossroads, looking toward the tree, which stays at frame-right. The 180° line is the line between the bend in the hedge and the tree; the camera stays on its side of that line.
FIRST FRAME: the supplied image, unchanged.

ACTION TIMING:
[0.00s–5.00s] [[ACTION]]
Nobody speaks in this shot.
PEOPLE: WARIN: a broad-shouldered, big-boned man in his late thirties with no fat on him, a square weather-beaten face with hollows under the cheekbones and cords in the neck, skin reddened by wind with broken capillaries on the cheeks and nose, old pockmarks, a wide nose slightly crooked, one eye narrower than the other, small dark eyes under thick brows, a sparse patchy dark-brown beard, unkempt at the chin, hacked short with a knife, greying in streaks; greasy dark hair, roughly cut; big scarred hands; he wears no mail, only a stained quilted gambeson with one sleeve patched in a different cloth, a cheap brown felt hat with a shapeless brim, a crossbow slung on his back, a quiver of bolts and a long knife at his belt, and a small cloth bundle sewn to the inside of his collar; mud to the thighs. || GIRART: a lean, hard man in his mid-fifties worn down by months of campaigning, upright in the saddle; a weathered oval face with high flat cheekbones and hollow cheeks, a straight nose, grey-green eyes under thick dark brows half gone grey, deep lines across the forehead and at the corners of the eyes, a short grizzled grey-and-brown beard hacked short with a knife, grey-brown hair in the thirteenth-century bowl cut with a straight fringe, pressed flat by the helmet, no modern haircut; a worn, stained sleeveless wool surcoat of faded madder red gone rusty brown, split for riding, with no charge, badge or embroidery, over a dark iron mail hauberk with mail sleeves and the frayed hem of a dull brown quilted gambeson, a plain leather sword belt with a long sword in a worn scabbard, scuffed leather riding boots; on the ring finger of his right hand a heavy man's signet ring of worn dull gold with a flat oval bezel engraved with a small shield of three diagonal bands and no border. Quiet authority, commands with a raised hand, never raises his voice. A distinct man from Bertran, Aymer and the Count.
CHARACTER ACTING: WARIN shoots like a professional and reloads without hurry, but his eyes never leave the man who is still walking with the bolt in him; the hands work, the face does not believe it. After the fight he unties the shovel and reads the ground: frozen ruts, then the soft black earth among the roots. He heads for the tree. At Odila's words he stops with the shovel raised and looks to Girart, and when Girart is looking elsewhere he drives the blade in between the roots.
GIRART commands without a word: his eyes go to the road behind, then to the crossroads, and his open right hand rises and the company spreads. He fights economically and without heat, striking once with the flat of the sword to end it. After the fight he steps down with a horseman's stiffness, takes in the dead, the road behind and the tree, then points: the dead, the ground, the road ahead. When Warin looks to him about where to dig, he keeps watching the road behind a beat too long, and lets the silence decide.
PHYSICS: Real weight: feet sink into soft mud and crack frozen ruts, breath steams, cloth and gear move with the body; any animal already in the first frame shifts its weight and blows.
LIGHTING: Early winter afternoon under a low, even overcast sky: flat, cold grey light with no sun and no hard shadows, frost in the wheel ruts, breath visible; the light falls slowly as the scene goes on.
STYLE: Photorealistic live-action medieval drama, thirteenth century, grounded and naturalistic, in open northern European farmland; muted desaturated palette, aged mud-stained costumes, no fantasy.
QUALITY: Photorealistic from frame zero; identities, costumes and animals consistent across the whole take; natural motion blur; no morphing.
